metaDescription: Penpot is an open-source design and prototyping platform that runs in the browser or on your own servers. See its features, cloud and self-host pricing, strengths, limitations and alternatives.
overview: Penpot is an open-source design and prototyping platform for product teams. Designers and developers work in the same browser-based workspace, with components, variants, shared libraries and interactive prototypes, and designs are built on open standards such as SVG, CSS and HTML.

You can use Penpot in the cloud or self-host it on your own infrastructure, including air-gapped environments. Layouts use CSS Flex and Grid, design tokens are built in, and the Inspect tab gives developers ready-to-use code. A free, open MCP server lets AI agents read and edit Penpot files.

features.title: Design and prototyping
features.text: Design interfaces in the browser and link screens into interactive prototypes to test flows.

features.title: Components and variants
features.text: Build design systems with components, variants and shared libraries, without plugins.

features.title: Native design tokens
features.text: Built-in tokens in the open W3C DTCG format, with token sets and themes.

features.title: CSS Flex and Grid layouts
features.text: Responsive layouts that follow the same rules as CSS, so designs map directly to code.

features.title: Inspect mode
features.text: Developers get SVG, CSS and HTML for any element from the Inspect tab, on every plan.

features.title: MCP server and plugins
features.text: A free, open MCP server connects AI agents to your files, alongside a plugin system and open API.

useCases: UI and UX design for web and mobile products
Design systems with tokens, components and variants
Teams that need self-hosting or data control
strengths: Open source, with the option to self-host on your own servers.
The free cloud plan includes all core design and prototyping features.
Built on open standards (SVG, CSS, HTML), so designs are close to production code.
Paid cloud pricing is predictable: the Unlimited plan is capped at $175/mo.
limitations: The free cloud plan is limited to 8 team members (viewers are unlimited) and 10 GB of storage.
Self-hosting requires a Linux server, Docker knowledge and managing the deployment yourself.
Free self-hosting comes with community support only.
SSO, a central admin console and audit logs need the Enterprise plan.
Runs in the browser only; there's no official desktop app.

pricing.summary: The cloud version has a free plan, and self-hosting the open-source version is free for unlimited users. Prices are in USD; discounts are available for non-profits, education and open-source projects.

plans.name: Professional
plans.note: Cloud · up to 8 team members, unlimited viewers · 10 GB storage · all core features

plans.name: Unlimited
plans.note: Cloud · capped at $175/mo for any team size · more storage · longer version history

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Cloud or self-host · SSO · central admin console · audit logs

plans.name: Private Server
plans.note: Dedicated infrastructure · custom hosting · enterprise-grade support

plans.name: Self-host
plans.note: Unlimited users, teams and files · community support · you run the server
